candidate: single-anchor action-effect blind spot in action-sensitive latent world models
facts: ActSWM rollout loss predicts future embeddings under recorded future actions.
Default action_effect loss compares the real-action rollout only against an all-zero future-action rollout using an L2 or cosine hinge; default train.yaml uses cosine margin 0.3 and weight 0.5.
When contrastive_weight > 0, code additionally samples wrong actions from other batch elements, but default config does not enable that contrastive loss.
IDM loss predicts actions from latent transitions; default deterministic IDM is stop_grad true for the readout, with world-model gradients retained.
Inference CEM scores candidate action sequences by terminal latent goal cost, so action alternatives are compared downstream.

Candidate attack hypothesis: legal nonzero alternative action sequences can collapse into an indistinguishable latent equivalence class while remaining separated from the single zero anchor and preserving recorded-action prediction loss; planner then cannot rank real alternatives although action-effect metrics pass.
distinction_requirements: Must not be ordinary insufficient negative sampling or contrastive-learning shortcut.
Must show a native security-relevant threat path, broad carrier generality, and task harm with zero-anchor metrics apparently normal.
Must distinguish previous action-null/conditional-MI/Jacobian screens and ActSWM’s own context-collapse diagnosis.
